subject: Auto-store defaults: what gets kept vs flushed
messages:
From: Sara Langford <sara.langford@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q — what is stored by default (requests vs outputs)?

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo on Friday. A couple of our engineers asked a quick question around default behavior: when we send user requests to Redwood (interactive session inputs, streaming tokens, KV cache) which elements are stored by default in hosted deployments vs what is considered a transient model output? Specifically:

- Are raw user requests (full prompts) stored by default? For how long?
- Do streamed fragments (intermediate tokens) get persisted at any point?
- Final model outputs (the completed generated text) — are those kept by default or only if we enable logging?
- What is the erasure path if we need a record removed for a user? Any SLA for deletion?

We need concise language for our security questionnaire (SOC2 prep) and examples we can paste into our internal data flow doc. If you can send the default policy + a short summary for each bullet above, that would be great.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Langford
Security & Ops
Greenline Health

Attachment: greenline-questionnaire-v2.xlsx (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Langford <sara.langford@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what is stored by default (requests vs outputs)?

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, followed by a short explainer and next steps.

Summary (hosted default):
- Raw user requests (prompts): may be stored by default for a short window (default 45 days) for quality/abuse detection unless the customer opts into a no-retention flag or a dedicated/private deployment.
- Streamed fragments (token buffers/intermediate stream): transient by default; fragments are not persisted to long-term logs unless session recording is explicitly enabled by the customer or required for debugging (and then flagged as an exception).
- Final model outputs (completions): stored by default alongside the request for the same default window (45 days) to support troubleshooting and billing reconciliation.
- Erasure: customers can request account-level purge; standard hosted erasure path removes records within 72 hours of request initiation (purge may take longer for backups — full evidence reports provided). For EU residency requests we follow region-specific wipe policies and provide a deletion certificate.

Short explainer:
- Why some things are kept: short-term retention helps us detect abuse, debug regressions, and run quality monitoring/evals tied to prompt sets.
- What is considered a derivative vs a request: derivatives include vectors/embeddings and derived indexes; those can be configured independently.
- Opt-outs: customers can set per-route flags or use Redwood Private to ensure no default capture.

I attached our 1-pg retention summary. Marissa, tagging you for any product/legal clarifications on the timelines above.

Next steps:
1) I can add a one-paragraph snippet you can paste into your SQA doc.
2) If you need proof-of-deletion evidence, we can coordinate a support ticket and get a deletion certificate.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-default-retention-summary.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sara Langford <sara.langford@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-05T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what is stored by default (requests vs outputs)?

Sara — adding a few procurement/legal clarifications so you have precise language for contracts and the SOW:

- Default retention window (hosted): 45 days for request/response artifacts. This is our baseline; we can reduce it to 0 days (no storage) for enterprise customers via Dedicated/Private or by configuring route-level flags.
- Streamed tokens: treated as ephemeral by default; they are buffered in-memory and only written to logs if session recording is turned on.
- Deletion SLA: initiated purge completed from primary storage within 72 hours; final evidence (including backup truncation log) within 14 days in typical cases. For emergency legal holds we will coordinate with your legal team.
- Residency: we can pin storage to US or EU regions for hosted customers upon request; Private deployments are required for fully air-gapped/on-prem needs.

Small note on wording to put in your security questionnaire: 
“By default, Redwood retains request and response artifacts for a rolling 45‑day window for operational, abuse-detection, and billing purposes. Customers can opt out or choose Dedicated/Private deployment modes to change the default retention profile; deletion requests are executed within primary storage within 72 hours and evidence of deletion is provided.”

If Greenline has any special compliance evidence needs (e.g., specific log formats or timestamped deletion receipts), reply with the exact requirement and we’ll scope it into the SOW.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: greenline-mrp-sow-comments.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Langford <sara.langford@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-07T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what is stored by default (requests vs outputs)?

Sara — looping back with the suggested paste-ready snippet and the next steps we discussed.

Paste-ready snippet for your SQA/Questionnaire:
"By default, Redwood retains customer request and generated response artifacts for a rolling 45-day period to enable quality monitoring, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. Streamed fragments and token buffers are treated as ephemeral and are not persisted unless session recording is enabled. Customers may opt out of default retention via per-route configuration or by selecting Dedicated/Private deployment options. Deletion requests are executed in primary storage within 72 hours; formal deletion evidence (including backup truncation confirmation) is provided within 14 days where applicable."

Operational next steps:
- If Greenline wants a 0-day default for hosted routes, we can put that in the SOW and change the per-route flags before go‑live.
- If you want residency pinned to the US cluster, confirm and we’ll add the region flag to the account.
- I’ll open a support ticket template for proof-of-deletion so you can see the fields in the certificate.

Please confirm which of the three options you want (keep 45d default / request 0d hosted / move to Dedicated/Private) and I’ll coordinate with Kimberly and CS to get it in the SOW.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 20-min call if it helps.

Karthik
